card.title: How To Fix iPhone X That Has No Touch

source.title: How To Fix iPhone X That Has No Touch

claims.statement: iPhone X no touch is most often sandwich separation between top layer and interposer: OL lines at touch connector J5800 point to it; test in an iSocket and reball.

Sometimes the bottom board is damaged (often near the SIM slot); a bottom board swap requires moving the baseband CPU, the baseband EEPROM (copy with JC module reader; losing it kills cellular forever), optionally NFC, and unbinding Wi-Fi via Purple Mode.
PP5V25_TOUCH_VDDH should read about 0.643 in diode mode; a low reading like 0.235 or a short often means C5645 (4 µF 6.3 V 0201) needs replacing.
Qualcomm (A1865) and Intel (A1901, A1902) boards must not be mixed when swapping bottom boards.

procedure: Test with only screen, port and battery connected.
Split sandwich; test in iSocket; reball if touch returns.
Pair it with a working bottom board that has the same modem type; swap paired parts if needed.
Check PP5V25_TOUCH_VDDH (~0.643); replace C5645 if low.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Overwriting or losing the baseband EEPROM data permanently kills cellular.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
